title: A Monte Carlo Approach to the Worldline Formalism in Curved Space
abstract: Develops a numerical method to evaluate worldline path integrals on curved Euclidean spaces sampled with Monte Carlo techniques. Modifies the YLOOPS algorithm with a quadratic stabilizing term to improve convergence. Tests on D-dimensional maximally symmetric spaces. Treats non-flat metric effects as interaction terms. Uses time-slicing discretization relative to proper time. Validated against analytical heat kernel calculations. Published in JHEP 11 (2020) 169.
key_claims: First numerical worldline Monte Carlo on curved Euclidean spaces
Works on D-dimensional maximally symmetric spaces (including D-spheres and D-hyperboloids)
Non-flat metric effects treated as interaction terms in perturbative expansion
Validated against analytical heat kernel calculations
Time-slicing discretization relative to proper time parallels quantum path integral construction
CRITICAL for HYP-2026-007: provides the methodology for worldline MC on hyperbolic lattice
